policy: Source-verified updates only. An hourly check may read approved machine-oriented official feeds, but new editorial entries require a primary source and a material change. Devpost observations are manual.

challenge.name: The WebMCP Challenge

updates.title: MCP adds an Infrastructure Working Group charter
updates.summary: Commit c7400a0 merges an Infrastructure Working Group charter into the official MCP specification repository. Builders and maintainers can now track this infrastructure-focused governance work in the repository; this is broader MCP ecosystem governance, not a protocol release or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: MCP repairs invalid JSON in two documentation examples
updates.summary: Commit dc48f37 makes two official MCP documentation examples parseable: it adds a missing comma to an Image Content example and replaces curly quotes plus an invalid default in a legacy single-select schema example. Builders copying these examples should use the corrected JSON; this is broader MCP documentation maintenance, not a new protocol release or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: MCP corrects native-app loopback redirect guidance
updates.summary: Commit 00c3f2e changes the draft CIMD example to use the IPv4 and IPv6 loopback literals instead of localhost, aligning its native-app redirect URIs with RFC 8252 guidance. Authorization implementers should prefer explicit loopback addresses in equivalent examples; this non-normative MCP draft fix is not a protocol release or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: MCP marks the Skills extension as published
updates.summary: Commit 24efd6e updates the official MCP repository documentation to reflect the Skills extension's published status and track continuing work in extension issues. SDK and client builders can now distinguish the published extension from its ongoing implementation work; this is broader MCP extension work, not a new MCP protocol version or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: WebMCP defines tool activation and cancellation events
updates.summary: Commit f5645e9 adds ToolActivatedEvent and ToolCancelEvent interfaces to the experimental WebMCP draft. Implementers and conformance tests should track these named event types when modeling tool activation and cancellation; this is a draft interface change, not evidence of browser support or a W3C Standard release.

updates.title: WebMCP adds a debugging tool annotation
updates.summary: Commit 8a82bb7 adds a debugging member to ToolAnnotations in the experimental WebMCP draft. Tool producers and consumers that mirror the draft should review their annotation validation and serialization for the expanded shape; this is not a browser-support signal or a W3C Standard release.

updates.title: WebMCP documents Permissions Policy as a security mitigation
updates.summary: Commit df2d824 documents Permissions Policy as a security mitigation for the experimental WebMCP draft. Security reviewers and browser integrations should include policy configuration when assessing tool exposure; this documentation change does not itself establish universal browser support or make WebMCP a W3C Standard.

updates.title: MCP adds support tracking for the Skills extension
updates.summary: Commit 2997f33 adds an overview and support tracking for the recently merged Skills extension in the MCP specification repository. SDK and client builders now have an official repository location to follow implementation support; this remains broader MCP extension work, not a released protocol version or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: WebMCP validates tool names before descriptions
updates.summary: Commit cc45efc changes registerTool() so the experimental WebMCP draft validates a tool's name before its description. Implementers and conformance tests should account for the resulting error order when both fields are invalid; this is a draft behavior change, not a W3C Standard release.

updates.title: MCP repository merges the Skills Extension proposal
updates.summary: Commit 1eb5bbe merges SEP-2640, titled Skills Extension, into the MCP specification repository. Agent and SDK builders now have a repository-level extension proposal to track, but this is not a released protocol version or a WebMCP browser change.

updates.title: WebMCP broadens executeTool() input to any value
updates.summary: Commit 97da8f5 changes the WebMCP draft's executeTool() inputObject type from object to any. Implementers that mirror the draft's interface definitions should review generated bindings and validation assumptions; this is a draft API change, not a W3C Standard release, and WebMCP remains experimental.

updates.title: WebMCP adds origin to observed-tool maps
updates.summary: Commit 94c0a3a includes origin information in the observation tool map through the observed tool collection structure. Clients consuming observed tools should preserve this provenance when distinguishing tools from different origins; the change is part of the experimental WebMCP draft, not a browser-support claim or W3C Standard release.

updates.title: MCP repository merges a filesystems working-group proposal
updates.summary: Commit aa8ce04 adds a proposal for a dedicated filesystems working group to the MCP specification repository. Filesystem implementers now have a governance effort to track, but this is a proposal rather than a released protocol change, and it belongs to the broader MCP ecosystem rather than the experimental WebMCP browser API.

updates.title: WebMCP explicitly brings headless handoffs into scope
updates.summary: Commit 50c4b7f moves headless browsing scenarios into the proposal's stated goals when page-exposed tools support task completion or transitions between human-in-the-loop and headless experiences. It still excludes purely server-side autonomous workflows and continues to position WebMCP as complementary to backend MCP; WebMCP remains an experimental Community Group draft, not a W3C Standard.

updates.title: WebMCP adds a consequential-action annotation
updates.summary: Commit 7b3f50f adds the consequentialHint tool annotation so clients and agents can identify actions with significant, real-world, or non-reversible effects and apply confirmation safeguards. The annotation is a signal rather than an enforcement mechanism; WebMCP remains an experimental Community Group draft, not a W3C Standard.

updates.title: WebMCP implementation status adds agent support
updates.summary: Commit 55fb7ee updates the draft report's implementation-status material to include agent support, and the canonical Community Group Report is now dated September 2, 2026. This is implementation-status evidence, not proof of support in every agent or browser; WebMCP remains an experimental Community Group draft, not a W3C Standard.

updates.title: Challenge organizers publish the halfway build checklist
updates.summary: The latest Devpost update asks builders to verify registered tools, a complete core flow, a deployed app, a public licensed repository, and a clear demo plan before the September 3 deadline.

updates.title: WebMCP Community Group Report dated August 26
updates.summary: The August 26 report defines the imperative browser API, lifecycle and exposure concepts, agent interaction model, and a growing security and privacy section. It remains a Community Group draft, not a W3C Standard.

updates.title: Chrome publishes a practical WebMCP tool-building guide
updates.summary: Chrome's guide walks through imperative registration, input schemas, tool results, annotations, state synchronization, feature detection, and cleanup for application developers.

updates.title: MCP maintainers publish a new protocol roadmap
updates.summary: The broader MCP project highlights agentic messaging, HTTP transport hardening, agent identity, enterprise security, improved primitives, and SDK experience. This is MCP ecosystem news, not a WebMCP browser API change.

updates.title: Cloudflare describes a remote-browser path to WebMCP
updates.summary: Cloudflare presents an approach for adding a WebMCP interface around existing sites with Browser Rendering and Workers. Treat it as one implementation pattern, not a change to the browser specification.

updates.title: MCP 2026-07-28 specification release ships
updates.summary: The broader MCP protocol release introduces a stateless core, discovery, cacheable list results, authorization hardening, and an extensions framework. WebMCP applications should track it for ecosystem alignment, but it is a separate specification.
